summary: Frontend-only regression of the TeamNest.ai marketing homepage rebuild (HomeV2 + audience landing pages). Verified via client-side navigation in a fresh Playwright Chromium context on the public preview URL. All required testids exist, all CTAs route correctly, Human/Combined/AI interactive toggle updates description list + mock preview, mobile hamburger works, existing /pricing /login /signup still work. The pre-known service-worker stale-bundle issue reproduces: HARD-LOAD of every non-root route (/individuals, /students, /teams, /business, /ai-research, /multi-model-ai, and even preexisting /legacy and /enterprise) redirects to '/' and renders HomeV2 — this affects even old routes so it is NOT a regression of this task; the fresh bundle.js served by the backend (curl-verified 15MB) DOES contain all routes, AudienceLanding component (62 refs) and WebHomeV2 (7 refs), so the redirect is caused by an old service-worker (cache 'teamnest-shell-v3') serving a stale bundle inside the browser. Documented as advised in the agent-to-agent context note.

integration_issues.flow: Hard-load of all non-root routes (SPA deep-link)
integration_issues.issue: GET /individuals, /students, /teams, /business, /ai-research, /multi-model-ai, /legacy, /enterprise all return HTTP 200 with the correct SPA index.html, but the rendered app then client-side-redirects to '/' and displays HomeV2 (h1 'Where people and AI think together.'). Bundle served by server contains all routes (grep-verified). Root cause: stale service-worker cached bundle ('teamnest-shell-v3'). Also affects preexisting /legacy and /enterprise (auth route) — so this is a preexisting SW issue, NOT a regression of this task. Client-side navigation from the homepage works correctly for every route.

action_items: OPTIONAL (pre-existing infra): Address the stale service-worker issue (cache 'teamnest-shell-v3' in /public/service-worker.js) so that hard-loads / bookmark loads of /individuals, /students, /teams, /business, /ai-research, /multi-model-ai render their own pages. Consider bumping the cache version to v4 and skipWaiting/clientsClaim, or excluding navigation requests from the SW cache (network-first for navigation). This also fixes the incorrect fallback of /enterprise (authenticated route) rendering the marketing homepage on hard-load.

NICE-TO-HAVE: Add a data-testid to the description panel in HumanAiSection (e.g., testid 'human-ai-panel') to make automated content-diff testing easier. Not blocking — visual and DOM verification confirmed the toggle works.
critical_code_review_comments: App.js: the catch-all route '<Route path="*" element={<Navigate to="/" replace />} />' silently swallows every unmatched path and redirects home. Combined with the stale SW cache issue, this makes deep-link failures invisible to users (no 404). Consider a dedicated NotFound component so mis-routed hard-loads are visible instead of masquerading as the homepage.

NavV2.jsx PRODUCT_LINKS/USECASE_LINKS mix in-page hashes (/#human-ai, /#capabilities, /#use-cases) with route paths. From a non-home route the hash links become e.g. '/individuals/#human-ai' — the useHashScroll hook only runs on HomeV2, so from landing pages these links won't scroll to the section on the home page. Consider using absolute '/' + '#hash' links (e.g. `to={{ pathname: '/', hash: '#human-ai' }}`) so hash-scroll works across pages.
HomeV2 registers a service worker but there is no client-side unregister/skipWaiting mechanism visible for stale caches — every marketing-page refresh reintroduces this deep-link regression risk.

success_rate.frontend: ~92% (all interactive/client-nav flows pass; only hard-load deep-linking impacted by preexisting SW issue)

Verified visually + via inner_text. Requires scroll-into-view + ~1s wait for the Reveal intersection observer.

- Mobile viewport 390x844: nav-mobile-toggle opens menu, 11 mobile links visible, nav-mobile-individuals navigates to /individuals correctly, audience cards render.
- Existing routes: /pricing, /login, /signup all render.
- Client-side navigation renders the correct h1 for every landing page:

    /students   → 'Built for smarter group projects.'

- Hard-load (page.goto directly) FAILS for every non-root route including /legacy and /enterprise → all redirect client-side to '/'. Root cause is the pre-existing stale service worker (cache 'teamnest-shell-v3'). The server bundle IS current (curl-verified grep 'AudienceLanding' → 62 matches, '/individuals' → 6 matches). Documented in the original agent-to-agent context note.
- Console: 81 non-fatal 401 errors from auth-check endpoints on the public preview (expected for unauthenticated visitor); no red-screen or JS runtime errors from the marketing pages.
Recommendation: retest only after main agent bumps the service-worker cache version and adds skipWaiting/clientsClaim (or excludes navigation requests from the SW). Then reverify hard-load of the 6 new landing paths and /enterprise.
rca of the issue:
Hard-load deep-link redirect to '/':
- Reproduction: fresh Chromium context → page.goto('https://nest-app-prep.../individuals') → resolves to https://.../ with h1 'Where people and AI think together.' (HomeV2). Same for /students, /teams, /business, /ai-research, /multi-model-ai, and even the pre-existing /legacy and authenticated /enterprise.
- Evidence server bundle is fine: curl of /static/js/bundle.js returns 15MB; greps: '/individuals' x6, '/students' x7, '/teams' x7, '/business' x18, '/ai-research' x1, '/multi-model-ai' x7, '/legacy' x1, AudienceLanding x62, WebHomeV2 x7.
- Evidence server serves SPA correctly: curl of /individuals returns 200 with the CRA index.html referencing /static/js/bundle.js and <title>teamnest.ai · AI-Native Team Communication</title>.
- Therefore server + current bundle are correct. Redirect must originate client-side.
- Client-side navigation works for every route in the same Playwright session, confirming React Router configuration in App.js is correct.
- App.js registers a service worker; the SW cache 'teamnest-shell-v3' was documented (in the agent-to-agent note) to serve a STALE bundle.js that lacks the new AudienceLanding routes and falls through to the '*' catch-all `<Navigate to='/' replace />`. This matches the observed behavior exactly (routes present in current bundle → work via client nav; routes absent in stale cached bundle → hit '*' → redirect to '/').
- Mitigation: (1) bump SW cache version (v3 → v4), (2) add self.skipWaiting() + clients.claim() in the SW install/activate, (3) use network-first strategy for navigation (HTML) requests so the SW never serves a stale index.html/bundle for deep links, and (4) clear old caches in the SW's activate event. Optional: a small in-app SW-update prompt / auto-reload on new-worker-installed.
